doc.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025

title: Nina Simone and musicians living overseas
summary: Musicians who went abroad, including Carmell Jones, Mal Waldron, and Abbey Lincoln's Italy tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. It does, it does. And it really comes out of the old spirituals when people were singing and hopes for and prayers for a better day, better conditions. I saw a heart wrenching interview, I mean sometimes stuff just pops up on YouTube and I say, “Oh I’ve just got to hear this,” something popped up the other day, somebody interviewed Nina Simone after she had left the States and went to France I think when she came back and they were interviewing her. And they asked her, you know, “Why did you leave?” And she says, “I left because I didn’t like this country. I didn’t like the way they were treating me. I didn’t like the way they were treating my people you know. And I came back because I thought things might be different you know, and she just really bared her soul and went on in this interview, went on about — I had to stop watching it. I’ll get back to it now because you know, the stories she’s telling is like so many other musicians who went overseas and then having lived overseas I had a chance to, I know when I was in Berlin one time I ran into Carmell Jones and Leo Wright. And they were saying, “Oh no, we ain’t never going back there, man, no we like it just fine here, you know Berlin is all right.” When I toured Italy with Abbey Lincoln, which that was an amazing band because Mal Waldron was the piano player you know, and Mal and I got pretty tight you know because he found out I could play chess and he loved to play chess you know so in addition to the music we — if we weren’t playing music we were playing chess you know. And so he said the same thing, “Na, na, na I’m not going back there.” And Art Farmer lived overseas for a while, Idris Muhammad, and even the old guys, Louis Armstrong, Coleman Hawkins, you know because you know things are just different. Musicians and artists are given another level of respect. You don’t make a ton of money but you get treated like somebody special which is something I think all artists need to do to encourage them to continue in their art.
